title: Observation record
description: Chapter 1's real output. A PERSONAL PREPAREDNESS OBSERVATION — not a critical-service map, not an assessment, not facility evidence. Canon: 'No formal assessment or transfer artifact is completed in Chapters 1-3.' The six boundaries below are what distinguish this from the artifact canon prohibits; if any is violated, this is the prohibited artifact with a new noun on it. R4 B4, DEC-008.

participantRef.description: ★ BOUNDARY 1 — PARTICIPANT-OWNED. Keyed to the person, never to the facility. A record keyed by facility is facility evidence whatever it is called, and it would survive the participant leaving in the wrong direction.

visibility.description: ★ BOUNDARY 1 — PRIVATE UNTIL DELIBERATELY PROMOTED. A `const`, not an enum: there is no other value to set. Not visible to a coordinator, not visible to the facility.

sections.description: ★ BOUNDARY 4 — the last two are REQUIRED, and they are what make this an observation rather than a finding. Without them it asserts an assessed dependency, which is the artifact.

undocumentedDependency.description: The product delivered once: 'What is keeping your service running that is not written down?'

notSureAbout.description: REQUIRED. 'What would you need to check before treating this as established?'

questionToAsk.description: REQUIRED. 'Who would you ask, and what would you ask them?'

exportLabel.const: unverified personal preparedness observation — not an assessment
exportLabel.description: ★ BOUNDARY 5 — carried on every export, alongside the scope-boundary statement. A `const` so it cannot be softened, shortened or localised into something that sounds like a finding.

promotion.description: ★ BOUNDARY 6 — the ONLY route into Chapter 4's facility-owned artifact, and it requires explicit confirmation and correction. ⚠️ Q19 owes who initiates it, who sees the record before and after, whether the participant may withdraw first, and what provenance survives. Until then this stays null.

provenance.description: Where in the fiction this came from. A reference, never a copy.

$comment: ★ BOUNDARIES 2 AND 3 ARE ENFORCED BY ABSENCE PLUS additionalProperties:false. There is no reviewState, no approvedBy, no completeness, no evidenceStatus, no capabilityCredit, no recognition and no flag property anywhere in this schema — so a record carrying one is UNREPRESENTABLE, not merely refused. That is stronger than a rule: a rule can be forgotten at the call site, and this shape has no room for the mistake. contracts/rules/observation-record.test.js asserts each absence by name, so adding one is a failing test rather than a silent widening.
